I am 45 years old, and I have been farming these 8 mu of land in Quzhou since I was young. My father taught me, and I finished middle school, so I can read and follow the guidance from the county ag-tech station. Around here, if you don't grow winter wheat followed by summer maize, you are throwing money away — this is the North China Plain, and the double-cropping system is what our land and climate are built for. Wheat goes in around early October after deep rotary tillage, and maize goes in right after the wheat comes out in June, usually no-till direct seeding because there is no time to waste between crops.

This year, I will stick with what works. For wheat, I will plant Luyuan 502 — it is the variety most of my neighbors trust, good resistance and stable yield. For the summer maize, I will use Denghai 605 hybrid seed. It costs more than traditional seed, but the yield difference pays for itself several times over, and every household around here uses it.

For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer as a base for both crops and top-dress with urea at the key growth stages. Wheat needs more phosphorus upfront for root development, so I apply about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Maize is similar in nitrogen demand but a bit less on phosphorus — around 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Irrigation depends on the rainfall, but wheat normally needs four good irrigations: winter water, jointing stage, heading stage, and grain filling. Maize usually gets by with two — one right after sowing to ensure emergence, and one at the big喇叭口 stage. For pesticides, I spray when I see problems or when the station warns us — usually about three times for wheat and three times for maize, covering herbicide, insecticide, and fungicide.

I expect my wheat to yield around 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates, and the maize should give me about 580 kg per mu. I am not experimenting with cotton or vegetables this year — they are too risky and need too much labor. Grain prices are stable, and I know these two crops.
